matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral to its integer value and compute the difference between the left‑hand side and the right‑hand side of the equation; this tells you how far the equality is off.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before exploring any stick moves, calculate the numeric values of both sides to know the exact adjustment needed.
matchstick.example: Incorrect pattern: Not calculating the numeric values before moving a stick, leading to a non‑balanced equation.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Enumerate every way a single matchstick can be relocated from a source character to a different destination character, making sure both source and destination remain valid symbols after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When generating candidate solutions, first list all possible single‑stick relocations before evaluating their effects.
matchstick.example: Incorrect pattern: Guessing a single‑stick move without considering all source‑destination possibilities.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate stick move, compute how the numeric values of the affected numerals change and check whether the net change matches the discrepancy needed to balance the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After enumerating moves, filter those whose numeric effect equals the required difference between the two sides.
matchstick.example: Incorrect pattern: Choosing a stick move that changes symbols but does not correct the numeric imbalance.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via equals
matchstick.principle: Treat the '=' sign as two horizontal sticks; moving one of them can turn it into a '-' while the other remains, or adding a stick can turn it into a '+'. The source operator must stay valid after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the needed numeric adjustment can be achieved by changing the equality operator, consider moving a horizontal stick from or to '='.
matchstick.example: Incorrect pattern: Removing both horizontals from '=', deleting the equality sign instead of converting it to a valid operator.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: A '+' consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; moving the vertical stick turns it into '-', and moving the horizontal stick can change it to other operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When you need to change a '+' to '-' (or vice versa), move the appropriate stick rather than adding or deleting sticks.
matchstick.example: Incorrect pattern: Changing a '+' to '-' without moving the vertical stick, resulting in an invalid operator.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑operator stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A stick can be transferred directly from one operator to another, simultaneously altering both operators (e.g., swapping a horizontal stick between '=' and '-'). Both operators must remain valid after the move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a single stick move can modify two operators to achieve the required numeric change.
matchstick.example: Incorrect pattern: Moving a stick from one operator but leaving the source operator invalid.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑numeral stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If adding a stick to a numeral would increase its value by the needed amount, consider moving a stick from an operator (such as '-' or '=') to that numeral, while keeping the operator valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy matches the value increase obtainable by augmenting a numeral with an extra stick.
matchstick.example: Incorrect pattern: Adding a stick to a numeral from an operator but not ensuring the operator stays a valid symbol.

matchstick.title: Inter‑character stick relocation (source may become empty)
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from one character to another, verify that the source character remains a valid Roman numeral or operator after the removal (or is eliminated only if it is a single‑stick numeral like I).
matchstick.when_to_apply: During candidate generation, discard any move that leaves the source character invalid.
matchstick.example: Incorrect pattern: Removing a diagonal from an X, leaving it as a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Numeral elimination via stick removal
matchstick.principle: A single‑stick numeral (I) can be removed by moving its stick to another character, effectively deleting the numeral from the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the required numeric change is a reduction of one, consider eliminating an I by relocating its stick.
matchstick.example: Incorrect pattern: Removing an I but forgetting to adjust the rest of the equation to maintain balance.

matchstick.title: Equation structure preservation
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, the equation must still contain exactly one '=', and each side must have at least one numeral and any required operators; never drop or merge characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before finalising a candidate solution, check that the overall equation syntax (left side, '=', right side) is intact.
matchstick.example: Incorrect pattern: Producing an answer that omits the '=' sign or one side of the equation, such as 'X - XI - V'.

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick without checking whether the source character still forms a valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each proposed stick move, verify that both the source and destination characters are valid symbols; only move sticks from characters that can lose a stick while staying valid.

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on making a syntactically plausible equation but does not compute the numeric values to ensure the equality holds.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Re‑calculate the integer values of both sides after any transformation and confirm they are equal before outputting the answer.

matchstick.description: Dropping or omitting parts of the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes an operator, numeral, or the equality sign while moving a stick, violating the requirement to keep the equation structure intact.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Maintain exactly one '=', and ensure each side still contains at least one numeral; never delete characters unless eliminating a single‑stick numeral (I).

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model changes an operator (e.g., '-' to '+') without considering how that alters the arithmetic result.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When modifying an operator, recompute the expression to see how the sign change affects the total and ensure the new equation can be balanced.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model proposes transformations that would require adding or removing more than one stick, such as turning X into I, which needs multiple sticks.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Count the sticks removed from the source and added to the destination; the net change must be exactly one stick moved.
